messages:
anya: Heads-up — after converting qwen-14b -> gemma-format + int4 quant, we see a small but repeatable regression on our rerank suite. MRR down 0.72 -> 0.68. Suspect token-id alignment / rotary handshake.
priya: ouch. any quick repro artifacts? model sha / conversion command?
sam: can you paste the top-of-run logs + a tiny example where outputs diverge? we should check KV-cache alignment (off-by-one BOS) and tokenizer id remapping.
anya: paste logs below, trimmed. noticed a pattern: cache misses spike at step 1 for long context.
```
INFO convert.py: starting conversion qwen-14b -> gemma
INFO tokenizer: loaded vocab size=50720
INFO tokenmap: applied mapping offset +1 for special tokens
WARN kvcache: unexpected token_id 2 at cache index 1
EVAL rerank: MRR 0.68 (baseline 0.72)
METRIC kl_token_dist=0.012
```
priya: the `applied mapping offset +1` line stands out. did the converter assume BOS=1? Qwen tokenizer uses BOS=0 afaik.
sam: yep. if converter increments special token ids to avoid collisions, that can shift all positions. rotary relies on token positions (via kv indexing) to align headwise rotations, so a systematic shift could change attention geometry.
anya: i dumped token ids for a failing prompt. two variants: original qwen tokenizer vs converted gemma tokenizer: `qwen: [0, 523, 12, 45...]` vs `gemma-conv: [1, 524, 13, 46...]` — everything +1.
priya: that explains it. even a +1 shift for the prefix would move cached keys' positions by one step during generation. did you try a local hack to subtract 1 before caching?
sam: before doing hacks, try a conversion flag: `--scrub-token-ids` vs `--preserve-specials`. converter CLI has forgotten to preserve BOS when target tokenizer had same sentinel. run with `--preserve-specials` and re-quantize.
ci-bot: build/conv-artifact/4033000000 created: https://ci.redwood/inference/artifacts/conv-4033000000.tar.gz (includes tokenizer.json, tokenmap.diff, quant-params.json)
anya: thanks, pulling now. Quick smoke: re-run rerank with conv-4033000000 + int4 params (scale=0.75). results: MRR 0.71, kl_token_dist=0.004. So preserving specials recovered most quality.
priya: nice. do we know why the converter default did +1? config mismatch? maybe a dev default for older gemma that assumed BOS=1.
sam: likely. we should add a strict unit test: assert roundtrip(tokenizer) preserves special token ids when formats are semantically equivalent. e.g. `pytest tests/tokenmap_test.py::test_bos_index_preserved`.
anya: opened a tiny patch: `conversion: default preserve_specials=True when source.specials intersect target.specials` — diff snippet:
```diff
- tokenmap.apply_offset_if_collision()
+ if source.specials & target.specials:
+     tokenmap.preserve_specials()
+ else:
+     tokenmap.apply_offset_if_collision()
```
priya: also add a canary rollout plan: serve converted model behind canary tag, route 0.5% of traffic, monitor per-route MRR and token-kl. auto-fallback to hosted qwen if MRR drops > 1.5% for 10m.
sam: add CI check for quantization noise too: run 200-sample rerank smoke to check MRR delta < 2% and KL < 0.01 before promotion.
anya: action items: 1) land converter patch + unit test (anya) 2) publish conv-artifact with preserve flag and run quant smoke (anya) 3) add CI smoke gate (sam) 4) canary rollout + observability hook (priya). I'll post PR link when ready. :hammer_and_wrench:
priya: thanks. low-effort mitigation: add a quick post-conversion scrub tool that reindexes tokenizer mapping if shift detected (useful for older artifacts).
sam: agree. once PR merges let's re-run the full eval harness (2000 queries) overnight and check Evals dashboard. if numbers look stable we can promote.
ci-bot: job rerun queued: conv-validation-4033000000 (est ~45m)
anya: ping @priya when canary goes live, will keep an eye on token-level kl and per-route MRR heatmap.
priya: will do. :eyes:
